newsitem.title: SPAIN: TENNIS-SPANISH DUO MAKE WEAKENED GERMANY SUFFER.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SPANISH DUO MAKE WEAKENED GERMANY SUFFER.

text.p: Spain's Davis Cup captain Manolo Santana lavished praise on Carlos Moya and Alberto Costa after watching his players take a commanding 2-0 lead over Germany in the Davis Cup on Friday.
"I knew they had played well at the Australian Open, but I had no idea they would play at such an extraordinary level," said Santana.

The Spaniards each took less than two hours to complete straight-set wins over Marc Goellner and Hendrik Dreekman, who proved no match for the home team's clay-court experts in the absence of Boris Becker and Michael Stich.
The Spaniards also silenced a group of German fans in the crowd carrying a banner reading "Davis Cup (possible) without Becker and Stich."
Moya broke Goellner twice in the first six games and continued the form which took him to the final in Melbourne to win 6-4 6-3 6-3.
The match between Dreekman and Costa was more finely-balanced, with breaks for both players in the opening games, before Costa raced away with the second set and won 6-4 6-1 6-4.
"The key was concentration, I knew it was going to be difficult," said Costa, who acknowledged he had been boosted by the exuberant crowd in the stadium.
"The Davis Cup atmosphere helps you to be more motivated, you know how important it is not just for you but for other people."
Santana, himself a veteran of several Davis Cup campaigns, conceded he had his initial doubts about the choice of venue, which was specially constructed for the event.
"At first we weren't sure ... because we knew there would be lots of Germans here, but the public really got behind the team," said Santana.
A jubilant Santana even admitted he had had his differences with his players after Real Madrid lost an important soccer match to Barcelona -- the favourite team of all his players.
"What I've put up with since yesterday (for Thursday) is incredible," joked Santana, a Real Madrid supporter. "They threatened to withdraw if I celebrated a Real goal."
